Description: Linked parallel turns as an inline stop, not only a turn. ICP-certified coach Asha Kirkby teaches consecutive parallel turns as a way to slow down and stop on inline skates: each turn bleeds off speed, and a chain of them brings you to a halt. But fluidity comes only when the upper body is integrated into the movement and the rotation is correct and sufficient. When a three turn or a transition stays jerky on inline skates, the missing piece is usually above the skates. Illustration generated with AI.

Description: What flow skating is made of, and what to master first. ICP-certified coach Asha Kirkby says it is only a smooth, skilful stringing together of skills that creates a continuous glide. The first step is to master each skill separately on inline skates: crossovers forwards and backwards, transitions both ways, backwards slides, crossunders and pivots. Only then do you link them.
